crypto_key_name.description: Resource name of the KMS key to use. Only regional keys are supported. Format: 'projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/keyRings/{{key_ring}}/cryptoKeys/{{key}}'.
crypto_key_name.rationale: Specifies the customer-managed encryption key used by the KMS configuration to protect NetApp volumes. Platform policy can require this value to be non-empty without hardcoding or pinning a specific key.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the KMS configuration can be deleted. Preventing accidental deletion helps protect the encryption settings.

description.rationale: Adds information about the KMS configuration. It does not affect security.

labels.description:
Labels as key value pairs. Example: '{ "owner": "Bob", "department": "finance", "purpose": "testing" }'.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Helps organise resources using tags. It does not affect security.

location.description: Name of the policy location. CMEK policies apply to the whole region.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: Gives the KMS configuration a name. It does not affect security.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the resource. It is a project reference chosen by the team and is not a platform security policy target.
